text:
Matthew Tkachuk played only 31 games last season, and he is making up for lost time. He has 32 points in 23 games, 18 of them on the power play, and a nine-game point streak. He also has his brother now: Brady Tkachuk arrived from Ottawa in a June trade, and on Nov. 14 the two led Florida past St. Louis on the night the Blues honored their Hall of Fame father, Keith. An NDTV Sports headline had Matthew calling the tribute "Icing On The Cake."

The shape of his game has shifted. His own chances are down from last season (0.86 expected goals per 60 minutes against 1.49), but his assists are up, 25 already. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile among forwards, though from only six tracked games.

His scoring rate sits above the top of our talent range, so expect it to settle a little. The process is real, though: Florida takes 55.9% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, 6.7 points better than without him. The two-time Cup winner is driving play again.
headline: Matthew Tkachuk has become a playmaker
